market_question: Will the Republicans win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: The 2028 election is an open-seat race following a single Trump term. Historical party alternation suggests a slight Democratic tilt, but a 38.5% implied probability for Republicans is too low. A baseline of roughly 45% is more balanced given the uncertain future landscape and party parity in modern presidential elections. The market may overprice Democratic chances due to current anti-Trump sentiment.
evidence_points: Rare historical precedent: open seat after a one-term Republican president following a one-term Democrat.
Party parity in U.S. presidential elections tends to revert to near-even odds absent a strong candidate or economic crisis.
Prediction markets often overreact to short-term sentiment; 38.5% undervalues the Republican potential to recover before 2028.
